title: The Street Corner
sceneText:
The one who walked off has come back.

Three of you standing at the corner outside the Secretariat. Nobody proposes going anywhere else and nobody says they are leaving. The sun is very low, and there is still one band of light on the wall across the street, drawing upward.

{@thierry}“Sold out?”

You say you sold out.

{@thierry}“Last market of October.” He moves the bottle to his other hand. “Next month there is the National Day first, and after that the Kindling, and what gets sold then is different.”

When he says it, it does not occur to him that you may not be here. Or it does, and he does not say so.

{@thierry}“I am out and about every day, mind,” he says suddenly. “Not that it was my choice either.”

You ask what he means by that.

{@thierry}“In a count’s house the eldest son takes the estate and the second goes into the temple,” he says lightly, as though it were somebody else’s business. “By rights the third goes into the army, or marries somebody he does not know and moves a long way off. I did not want either road.”

{@thierry}“So I made the Duke laugh, at a hunt.” He opens a hand. “That is all. One post, and I earned it myself.”

Timothy has not spoken. Thierry turns to him.

{@thierry}“And you, Kessler. Three years now.”

{@timothy}“I was posted here.”

Thierry waits a moment to see whether more is coming. That is the whole of it, and nothing else.

{@thierry}“Posted here.” He repeats it. “So you spend every day working out when you get moved on.”

{@timothy}“The fifth year,” he says. “Usually the fifth year.”

The band of light finishes drawing up off the wall. The corner goes dim.

Thierry moves the bottle from one hand to the other, and then looks at you.

{@thierry}“And you, Steward,” he says. “I earned mine. He was posted. You came of your own accord.”

{@thierry}“So why do you want to stay here?”

choices.text: It is only a contract. Thirty days, and then I go

effects.logEntry: You said it was only a thirty-day contract.

choices.resultText:
{@thierry}“Right.”

He does not ask again. Neither does Timothy.

They stand a while longer, and then Thierry says it is getting dark and to mind the road. They go off in opposite directions.

You stand at the corner a few seconds before you remember that your cart is still on the east side of the square.

effects.logEntry: You said you needed the work.

choices.resultText:
{@thierry}“There is work everywhere.”

The forester says it without aggression; it is only said in passing. But neither the temporary steward nor the inspector picks it up.

Kessler looks up at the light and says he should be getting back.

As the three of you separate, Thierry says “see you next month”, but he knows that next month you may not be here.

choices.text: I … I want a standing of my own

effects.logEntry: At the street corner you said something you had not expected to say.

choices.resultText:
For several seconds after you say it, nobody speaks.

You hear what you said. Why you said it in front of an inspector and a forester you do not understand yourself.

And then Thierry laughs.

Loudly, with an echo in the emptied street. He waves a hand while he laughs, meaning that he is not laughing at you.

{@thierry}“Kessler,” he says, catching his breath. “Did you hear that?”

{@timothy}“I heard it.”

He puts a hand inside his uniform and takes out a card. Dark ground, a pattern pressed into it. You cannot make out what the pattern is; you can only see that it is not a plant.

{@timothy}“This is an identity card of the Crown Lands,” he says.

He holds the card up for you to see for a few seconds, and puts it away.

{@timothy}“Three years I have been here. People still look twice when it comes out.”

Timothy Kessler smooths the pocket flat.

{@timothy}“Everybody around here carries a Valewisp one. The sort with the grapevine. Martha’s, Gregor’s, Vallant’s, all of them,” he says. “They are not looking twice on purpose. It is only that they do not see this one about.”

A few seconds pass.

{@timothy}“It is not hard to stay in this country. Not harder than anywhere else, to be exact. What is hard is everything after staying.”

And then he goes back to reciting terms.

{@timothy}“On residence,” he says. “Renewal of a temporary permit requires the guarantor to sign again. It may be submitted within seven days of expiry, and residence remains valid while the application is under consideration; you do not become illegal by waiting for a result.”

{@timothy}“The first renewal is ninety days. After three consecutive renewals it becomes annual. At five years you may apply for long-term residence, and long-term residence is not nationality. And the Kingdom does not accept dual nationality.” He stops for half a second. “Nationality requires eight years, and a recommendation out of a local jurisdiction.”

{@thierry}“Eight years,” he says. “Then you will be busy.”

He has not finished.

{@thierry}“And there is a thing he left out.” He points a finger in Timothy’s direction. “When you apply you have to enter a duchy. What you get after eight years is not only the Kingdom of Marigni’s papers. It has to be some particular duchy’s as well.”

{@thierry}“So you will have to choose.”

He starts counting them off.

{@thierry}“Ridgecrest: six months of winter, you go out and never see the sun, hard people, hard drink. The Flamincore lot talk like men quoting a price; everything gets reckoned up first. Luminveil is all scholars, still arguing through dinner. Stormgale is on the sea, and does not ask where you are from.”

{@thierry}“The Crown Lands.” He shakes his head. “The Crown Lands are not a place to live a life.”

He has finished counting.

{@timothy}“And Charleville.”

{@thierry}“That one does not count, Kessler. That is the Throne’s as well. You know that.”

{@thierry}“So choose here.” He taps a finger against the bottle.

Then Thierry holds the bottle out. You take it. There is half of it left, and it is still warm.

{@thierry}“When people here ask where you are from,” he says, “it is because they actually want to know.”

They go off in opposite directions. A few steps on, Thierry looks back.

{@thierry}“Keep the bottle.”
